comparisons.peer_summary: The Company values inventory at standard cost, adjusted to the lower of actual cost or estimated net realizable value. It fully reserves for inventories and non-cancellable purchase orders deemed obsolete, and performs periodic reviews of inventory items to identify excess by comparing on-hand balances to anticipated usage based on historical activity and forecasted demand.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies explicitly state that inventory valuation involves significant judgments regarding future selling prices and demand to determine the lower of cost or net realizable value. However, while Micron highlights the sensitivity of write-downs to differences in projected future average selling prices, AMD details a broader set of assumptions including historical sales activity, specific obsolete reserves, and periodic reviews against forecasted demand.

sentences.text: As described in the Inventories note to the consolidated financial statements, as of August 29, 2024, the Company had a net inventory balance for finished goods and work in process inventory totaling $8.1 billion.

As disclosed by management, determining the net realizable value of the Company's finished goods and work in process inventories involves significant judgments, including projecting future average selling prices, future sales volumes, and future cost per part.

Differences in future average selling prices used in calculating lower of cost or net realizable value adjustments can result in significant changes in the estimated net realizable value of finished goods and work in process inventories and accordingly the amount of write-down recorded.
The Company values inventory at standard cost, adjusted to approximate the lower of actual cost or estimated net realizable value using assumptions about future demand and market conditions.

In determining the lower of cost or net realizable value reserves, the Company considers assumptions such as recent historical sales activity and selling prices, as well as estimates of future selling prices.

The Company performs periodic reviews of inventory items to identify excess inventories on hand by comparing on-hand balances and non-cancellable purchase orders to anticipated usage using recent historical activity as well as anticipated or forecasted demand.

comparisons.peer_summary: Inventory is valued at the lower of actual cost (determined under FIFO) or net realizable value, with provisions for excess and obsolete inventory recorded based on forecasted product demand and production requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and scope of Critical Audit Matters
comparisons.peer_summary: Critical Audit Matters are matters arising from the current period audit that relate to material accounts or disclosures and involved especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the criteria for identifying a Critical Audit Matter (CAM). Micron identifies the net realizable value of inventory as a CAM due to 'significant judgment by management' and 'auditor judgment, subjectivity and effort' regarding future selling prices. Similarly, AMD defines CAMs as matters that relate to material accounts and 'involved our especially challenging, subjective or complex judgments,' establishing the same threshold for auditor attention to subjective financial estimates.

sentences.text: The principal considerations for our determination that performing procedures relating to the net realizable value of finished goods and work in process inventories is a critical audit matter are (i) the significant judgment by management in determining the net realizable value of finished goods and work in process inventories and (ii) a high degree of auditor judgment, subjectivity and effort in performing procedures and evaluating management's significant assumption related to future average selling prices.

The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective or complex judgments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose the specific impact of inventory write-downs on gross margin, including the counter-intuitive benefit of selling previously written-down inventory. MU reports that its 2024 gross margin was aided by 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023,' whereas AMD explicitly states as a general risk/policy that selling such inventory results in 'a net benefit to our gross margin' because revenue is recorded with 'a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales.'

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.
